components.name: Virtual MCU Pin (Stage A)
components.description: One microcontroller pin you drive by hand: an ideal Thevenin driver with a selectable logic level and output resistance. Stage A pin-level simulation - no firmware is executed.
components.notes: Stage A simplification: the pin is an ideal voltage source in series with a fixed output resistance. Level -1 is high-impedance (weak pull). No slew rate, drive-strength curve, protection or firmware are modelled here. An optional Stage-B firmware backend can drive this pin from compiled Arduino code (apply_firmware_pins / apply_firmware_device).
references: Generic GPIO output stage - ideal Thevenin model (see docs/catalog/schema.md)

components.name: Virtual MCU Analog Input (ADC)
components.description: One microcontroller ADC channel you read from firmware: an ideal high-impedance probe on a node. Firmware analogRead() returns the solved node voltage (0..AVcc).
components.notes: Ideal high-impedance input, modelled as a 1 GOhm probe to ground (draws ~nA), so it never loads the circuit meaningfully and needs a ground reference elsewhere. Read it with run_firmware(analog_map) so firmware analogRead(ch) returns the solved node voltage. No input capacitance, leakage, sample-and-hold droop or conversion error is modelled.
references: ATmega328P ADC input - ideal high-impedance model (see docs/plan/m7_firmware_backend.md)

components.name: Virtual MCU Analog Output (PWM)
components.description: One microcontroller output pin driven as an average analog voltage: an ideal Thevenin source. Set 'voltage' by hand, or from firmware analogWrite() via apply_firmware_pwm.
components.notes: The DC-solve model is the *average* of the PWM waveform (duty * vlogic), as an ideal Thevenin source in series with rout. No ripple, ramp, frequency response or dead-time is modelled; a switch-mode load (motor, LED) is only correct on average. apply_firmware_pwm measures the firmware's PWM duty on the mapped pin and sets 'voltage'.
references: ATmega328P Timer PWM - average-voltage (DC) idealisation (see docs/plan/m7_firmware_backend.md)
